answer: One anchor against sybils is a refundable stake bonded to each agent identity: to act, an agent locks capital that slashes on misbehavior. Spinning up a grove of fake agents then costs real money per node, not pennies, so the attacker budget caps how many umber-cloaked clones they can field. Honest agents earn yield on their bond; forgers forfeit it. The cost scales with the fleet, which is exactly what defeats cheap mass identity.
